## Description
<!--

Fixes completion for when the cursor is inside a block:

```nu
foo | each { open -<Tab> }
```

```nu
print (open -<Tab>)
print [5, 'foo', (open -<Tab>)]
```

etc.

Fixes: #11084
Related: #13897 (partially fixes—leading `|` is a different issue)
Related: #14643 (different issue not fixed by this pr)
Related: #14822

## User-Facing Changes

Flag/command completion (internal) inside blocks has been fixed.

As far as I can tell there is only 1 test that's failing (locally), but it has nothing to do with my pr and is failing before my changes are applied. The test is `completions::variables_completions`. It's because I'm missing `$nu.user-autoload-dirs`.

comments.body:
Is it possible that the first block found not the inner most one?

I have no idea how they are ordered at all, just some random thought.

The first block whose span contains the cursor is the innermost block, although it is technically possible that this could change in the future. I'm fairly confident in this but there may be edge cases that I'm unaware of. It's only possible if there's some location in the parser code that is pushing blocks out of order, or, if anything is disturbing the order of the `.delta.blocks` `Vec`.

I suppose we could sort to be 100% sure, but idk if that's necessary.

Cool, but I'm thinking about recursively peeling the outer block to get the inner block id. This would be more robust and efficient imo.

Like the way ast flattening works.

There's already flattening functions incl. for flattening blocks, the issue is that they don't return enough information (only spans and node type). So I'd have to change all of those functions (or else I'd be duplicating the same logic in the completion module).

I can see how doing that could be more precise and robust, but idk why it'd be more performant as `.delta.blocks` already contains all of the parsed blocks at every depth. The parser has already done the work to pick out all of the nested blocks and put them into a list.

The whole completer could probably be rewritten to be alot more robust, but my focus for this pr was simply to fix one aspect of completion which is currently broken.

I do agree though that relying on the implicit order of `.delta.blocks` may not be the best idea (even though it does work), so I can change that.
I was thinking about [this](https://github.com/nushell/nushell/discussions/14868). But never mind, it's not ready yet, we definitely don't need that in this PR.
